column1: # STATUS: LIVE, 2026-11-09. Rust tests that judge the REPOSITORY, not the product: each one reads documents,
# archived sources or cited evidence files that .workerignore deletes, so it cannot pass on the stripped tree and
# cannot be made to without keeping docs/, archive/ or large parts of traces/ (the md ignore line and the
# no-negation syntax make that impractical). They are claim and structure checks in the sense of the owner's
# stripped-tree rule: they run on the FULL tree, in the `stable` job (scripts/ci/full_tree_tests.py run), and the
# `stripped` job skips exactly these names (full_tree_tests.py skips). Nothing is dropped: a listed test that does
# not exist, or does not pass, fails `stable`; a test missing from this list fails `stripped`.
# Columns (tab separated): package, test target, test name, what it reads.
